image_description: A close-up, high-resolution shot of the head and upper jaw of a Nile crocodile. The image focuses on the textured, armored skin (scutes) around the eye and snout. The eye is visible with a vertical slit pupil. Several large, conical teeth are visible along the lower jawline, interlocking with the upper jaw. The skin texture is highly detailed, showing cracks and rough osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the snout tapers to a point, consistent with the V-shape of a crocodile rather than the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure appears broad and robust.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Multiple large, conical teeth are clearly visible protruding from the lower jaw and fitting into/notches of the upper jaw. The interlocking nature is evident.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is positioned on the top surface of the head. The pupil is a distinct vertical slit. The eye structure looks biologically accurate.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tip of the snout is cut off by the left edge of the frame; nostrils are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the full body isn't seen, the visible neck and head transition show heavy armor plating (osteoderms) consistent with an elongated, armored reptile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture shows distinct, raised, bony plates (scutes) with a rough appearance. While 'longitudinal rows' are hard to trace fully in this crop, the local arrangement is consistent with this pattern.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of sandy grey and brown, and the texture is visibly rough and cracked, matching the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows the dorsal/lateral side of the head and jaw. The ventral surface (belly) is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No limbs or feet are visible in this close-up crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is not visible in the frame.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Nile Crocodile vs. other crocodilians) based on fine-grained features like snout shape and tooth arrangement.
To analyze the complex texture of the scutes for any signs of AI-generated smoothing, repetition, or unnatural blending, which are common artifacts in reptile generation.
To ensure the teeth are distinct, solid objects properly embedded in the jawbone without melting or fusion artifacts at the gum line.

focus_areas: Structural integrity of teeth and jaw connection
Edge sharpness between subject and background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the texture of the skin. AI often fails to render the chaotic but structured nature of crocodile scutes, resulting in either overly uniform patterns or muddy, indistinct textures. Verify if the teeth look like separate solid objects or if they merge into the jaw. Check the eye for realistic depth and reflection.

metadata.class_label: African crocodile, Nile crocodile, Crocodylus niloticus
